Each entry carries a signature, parameter and returns tables, and an **executable example that renders the real frame** at build time. The MLB namespace ships ~116 `espn_mlb_*` callables in total; this page documents four. --- ## `espn_mlb_teams` ```python espn_mlb_teams(return_as_pandas: bool = False, **kwargs) -> pl.DataFrame ``` Look up the full MLB team directory from ESPN's Site v2 API. **Parameters** | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `return_as_pandas` | `bool` | `False` | If `True`, return a pandas DataFrame; else polars. | **Returns** — a tidy `polars.DataFrame`, one row per team: | Column | Type | Description | |---|---|---| | `team_id` | str | ESPN team identifier. | | `team_abbreviation` | str | Short team code (e.g. `LAD`). | | `team_display_name` | str | Full display name. | | `team_location` | str | City / location. | | `team_name` | str | Nickname. | | `team_color` | str | Primary hex color. | | `team_logos` | list | Logo asset records. | **Example** ::: {#c649bf30 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from sportsdataverse.mlb import espn_mlb_teams teams = espn_mlb_teams() print("shape:", teams.shape) teams.select(["team_id", "team_abbreviation", "team_location", "team_name"]).head(8) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` shape: (30, 14) ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
